apply_url.description: The posting's application address when it differs from source_url (http or https). Stored with the job; find_job_by_url then finds the job by it when the address names the posting (an id in its path or query). Without update, a saved job takes it only when it has none; with update it replaces the stored one.
apply_url.title: Apply Url

update.description: True: when the posting is already saved, this extraction replaces that job's fields and skills through the same mapping a new capture uses; the job keeps its id, status, applications, proposals, source and raw_text. It overwrites the stored extraction, which the web app can't undo. The saved job is found the way a capture finds it: resend the saved raw_text, or omit raw_text and pass its source_url (new raw_text misses the text match and creates a new job). The response's correction is {changed: the fields whose value changed, "skills" when the skill list did; scores_cleared: the job's match scores deleted because a field scoring reads changed, after which the job is scored again; rescored: true when that succeeded; rescore_failed: "bases" or the application ids it could not score, which score_ats computes later; tailored_applications: tailored resumes, left as written; open_sessions: open gap analyses, left to read as out of date, with their score link cleared; proposals_fit_stale: proposals whose stored fit predates the correction}. A job another copy of Maestro owns is refused (409). False (default): a repeat capture returns the saved job unchanged.
update.title: Update

ops.description: Typed edit ops. Each is an object with a `kind`, one of: replace_summary | toggle_entry | replace_bullet | replace_skills_group | add_skill_item | add_bullet | add_entry | replace_entry | remove_entry | remove_bullet | replace_contact | replace_certifications | add_extra_section | replace_extra_section | remove_extra_section | move_extra_section. To change a field ON an entry — dates, title, company, project name, link, tech — use replace_entry with that entry's index and the full edited entry object; it is scoped to that one entry (a whole-resume replace is the separate update_base_resume tool). See the tool description for each op's shape. add_extra_section/replace_extra_section `value` is {key,title,enabled,type:"entries"|"bullets"} plus EITHER entries:[{heading,subheading?,location?,date?,link?,enabled,bullets:[str]}] OR bullets:[str] — never both; unknown keys are rejected (400, extra="forbid"). Text the ops write is implied first person: a line with I/he/she/they or the owner's name is a 400 naming the lines, and nothing is written.
ops.title: Ops

formatting.description: Look settings to keep (keep=true), one object of the template knobs: font_size (10|11|12), side_margins and top_bottom_margin (0.3-1.0 inches), line_spacing (0.9-1.4), section_spacing (0-14 pt), entry_spacing (0-10 pt), justify and hide_divider (true|false), bullet_icon ("bullet"|"dash"), header_align ("left"|"center"|"right"), date_format ("verbatim"|"short_month"|"long_month"|"numeric"), education_order ("degree_first"|"institution_first"), skills_layout ("inline"|"bulleted"), section_order (a list of summary, experience, projects, extra_sections, skills, education, certifications; the rest follow in the template's order). It replaces the resume's saved look settings: a knob left out takes the template's default (on a tailored resume, its base resume's setting first), and {} clears them. An unknown knob or a value out of range is a 400 and nothing is kept. get_base_resume returns a base resume's saved formatting and template_id.
formatting.title: Formatting

keep.description: True: before rendering, the template_id and/or formatting given are saved on this base resume or tailored resume, so its later renders use them, after an edit too; template_id must name a ready template. False (default): template_id is a one-off for this render, the saved design is unchanged, and formatting is refused.
keep.title: Keep

document.description: "resume" (default): the tailored resume's PDF. "cover_letter": the PDF of the cover letter stored for the application (store_cover_letter or generate_cover_letter), rendered first when it has none, staged in the same folder under its own file name, so the two copies sit side by side. With no cover letter stored the call is refused and nothing is staged.
document.title: Document

view.description: top_skills: the most in-demand skills across the stored JDs, as {meta, top, rest}; meta.total_jobs counts the jobs read. heatmap: skill demand by role category, one row per skill and role with pct_jobs, the share of that role's jobs, and count of `of`, the role's jobs. role_mix: jobs by role category per week; every week from the first to the last has a row for every role, with count 0 where the role had no jobs. fit_distribution: how each base resume's match scores (deterministic engine) spread across jobs in five buckets; display_name is the resume's own name (null for a slug with no row), and the slug is an internal identifier. ats_over_time: the average match score per week, split by phase (base vs tailored) and role category. tailoring_lift: how much tailoring lifts the match score (base to tailored), averaged per role category, plus an overall row.
view.title: View

use_presets.description: True: once the session is created, fill it from the user's Quick tailor presets (get_tailoring_options explains them) through resolve_gaps' honesty-gated save path, deterministically and with no AI. The presets plan only mechanical, evidence-respecting moves; the fill does not write resume text. The returned resolutions_json may already resolve every gap, including system-planned entries (payload.provenance); a gap the presets do not decide is saved as skip. A session whose answers are all skip is not an error: the presets allowed nothing for it, and resolve_gaps still saves answers on it. An unverified or absent skill enters only a skills category (add_skill_item), never as an experience or project bullet; the server does not gate edit ops the caller writes against fabricated skills, experience, metrics or dates. A stale or no-longer-open session blocks the fill (409). The `next` hint then carries the presets' standing instruction as tailor_session's user_prompt when the session has no note of its own.
use_presets.title: Use Presets

resolutions.description: Batch of {gap_id, action, payload}. Actions: add_keyword | user_input | attach_project | skip | enable_entry | port_kb_point | cannot_confirm. Validated as ONE unit — one invalid item saves NOTHING (existing saved resolutions untouched). Merge-by-gap_id; omit never deletes — resend skip to retract. Payloads: add_keyword needs placement_target {section, index_or_category} (+ optional wording); a MISSING skill may use add_keyword ONLY with section=skills. user_input {text}. attach_project {project_name}. enable_entry {section: experience|projects, index}. port_kb_point {kb_point_id, kb_entity_id, placement_target, wording}. skip/cannot_confirm {} (cannot_confirm also stores a durable user_cannot_confirm KB record; only legal on gaps that ask a question, i.e. where user_input is allowed).
resolutions.title: Resolutions

no_new_text.description: True: Maestro writes no new wording and calls no model, whichever writer setting the user chose. It applies only the saved answers that need none: enable_entry, port_kb_point (an approved career-history bullet) and add_keyword into the skills list (keywords_added lists the words). An add_keyword placed anywhere else needs a rewritten line: its word lands in the skills list when the resume lacks it, and otherwise the answer is listed in answers_left_to_ops beside the user_input and attach_project answers; nothing listed there reaches the resume. With non-empty ops it is a 422; when nothing can be applied without new wording it is a 400 that says so.
no_new_text.title: No New Text

ops.description: Typed edit ops, the shapes edit_application's ops parameter lists; omitted (and no_new_text false), Maestro's AI writes them when the user's writer setting is Maestro's AI. With ops the server itself applies only the saved enable_entry and port_kb_point answers: user_input and attach_project answers reach the resume only through these ops, and answers_left_to_ops lists them. On every path a saved add_keyword whose word (its wording, else the gap's jd_skill) is not on the result is added to the skills list, in the category it chose, else Additional Skills, never as a bullet; keywords_added lists those words.
ops.title: Ops

file_path.description: An absolute path to an existing PNG or JPEG on this machine, typically as a browser tool reports it (Playwright MCP saves to its --output-dir; with the standard setup that is under the repo's .playwright-mcp/ tree, e.g. /Users/<user>/Projects/maestro-career-studio/.playwright-mcp/<name>.png); a relative or ~ path is resolved against this server's working directory. When this server runs inside the backend container, a host path with a `.playwright-mcp/` segment is read from the container's mount of that tree (paths that leave the tree are refused). PNG/JPEG only, 5 MB max.
file_path.title: File Path
